explanation: It is named after French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in 1912, and it creates hundreds of flavour compounds. Caramelization, by contrast, browns sugar on its own.

claims.text: The Maillard reaction between reducing sugars and amino acids browns toast, seared meat and roasted coffee beans.
Caramelization, oxidation and fermentation are not reactions between sugars and amino acids.
The Maillard reaction is named after the French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in 1912.
The Maillard reaction produces hundreds of different flavour compounds.
Caramelization is the browning of sugar by heat alone, without amino acids.
